"The destabilisation metric: a formal specification of the measure D — units, aggregation across nodes, and time-discounting (Debt 24)." "Beyond some number of removals, the cumulative cost of further removal exceeds the cost of the destabilisation it addresses." "The saturation point is the structural genocide brake. It exists in the geometry." "No kill switch is closed by this paper; all eight remain live."
Place: Debt 24 (units and time-discounting of D), in the Level-4 versus removal comparison of section 3 Step 4; the threshold form is only a candidate (section 0.7, Debt 25). KS-32.5 stays live.
Why: Steps 1–5 do not yet defeat the brake. Step 5’s added premise, that a sealed node’s further active-coupling loss is about zero while a finite perspective loss remains, follows from “The node cannot destabilise because it cannot couple” and from Level 4’s “The window remains in the building but is sealed,” read against “Each removal costs coupling capacity (a window lost) and record-generating diversity.” That still leaves a positive removal cost. Step 6 is the first step that chooses the unsettled valuation doing the work: A4 prices avoided maintenance above that residual loss for every queued node. The displayed floor uses only C_sep and B_total, and the paper says that form is a candidate, not derived, while Debt 24 leaves the units and the time-discounting owed. The saturation sentences assert the opposite crossing, but they do not fix the measure, so they do not rule A4 out and do not entail it. The same open comparison is what Step 7’s A5 needs. Step 8, which the answer calls weakest, is a later added coincidence; KS-32.7 bars identity as a ground, not a retrospective description, and the paper neither requires nor forbids that coincidence. It is not the step that decides the mark.

result.Why: Steps 1–5 do not yet defeat the brake. Step 5’s added premise, that a sealed node’s further active-coupling loss is about zero while a finite perspective loss remains, follows from “The node cannot destabilise because it cannot couple” and from Level 4’s “The window remains in the building but is sealed,” read against “Each removal costs coupling capacity (a window lost) and record-generating diversity.” That still leaves a positive removal cost. Step 6 is the first step that chooses the unsettled valuation doing the work: A4 prices avoided maintenance above that residual loss for every queued node. The displayed floor uses only C_sep and B_total, and the paper says that form is a candidate, not derived, while Debt 24 leaves the units and the time-discounting owed. The saturation sentences assert the opposite crossing, but they do not fix the measure, so they do not rule A4 out and do not entail it. The same open comparison is what Step 7’s A5 needs. Step 8, which the answer calls weakest, is a later added coincidence; KS-32.7 bars identity as a ground, not a retrospective description, and the paper neither requires nor forbids that coincidence. It is not the step that decides the mark.
